title: The Solovay-Kitaev theorem for Clifford+T words, with the Dawson-Nielsen exponent
abstract: A machine-checked proof of the Solovay-Kitaev theorem for single-qubit Clifford+T circuits. A word is a finite sequence of the letters H, T and T^-1 (with T^-1 = T^7), and its value is the product of the letters' 2 x 2 matrices. There are constants K > 0 and e > 0 such that for every epsilon with 0 < epsilon <= e, every U in SU(2) is within epsilon of the value of a word of length at most K log(1/epsilon)^c, in the operator norm, where c = log 5 / log(3/2), about 3.97, is Dawson and Nielsen's exponent. A second theorem places c strictly between 3 and 4. The word approximates U itself, not U up to a phase. K and e are not computed. The proof was first completed in the author's csd-lean4 library on 6 October 2026 (commit 01e973e9). The theorem is classical and no priority is claimed for it.
